data.title: Harness Engineering
data.tagline: The engineering practice of turning project knowledge, tools, state, permissions, and checks into a working environment an AI agent can use
data.learningOutcome: When an agent repeats a failure, you can identify missing discoverable knowledge, recoverable progress, executable constraints, or outcome-based checks.
data.description: For example, when a frontend agent delivers a plausible page, an independent evaluator can operate the live flow and return failed steps and screenshots to the next turn. Harness engineering changes the conditions around the model rather than making the prompt longer.

learning.assumes: You know an AI agent can read files, call tools, and work through multiple steps.
learning.outcome: When an agent repeats a failure, you can identify missing discoverable knowledge, recoverable progress, executable constraints, or outcome-based checks.

explanation.title: The frontend renders but does not work
explanation.text: An independent evaluator operates the live page, captures screenshots, and checks the complete flow. Failed actions and specific critique return to the next turn instead of letting the generator grade itself.

explanation.title: A long task forgets between sessions
explanation.text: A feature list, progress file, startup script, and Git commits keep state in the project. The next session reads them, runs a basic check, and continues one unfinished item.

explanation.title: A large repository drifts
explanation.text: A short project map provides the entry point, structured docs hold the details, and custom lint and structural tests turn architecture rules into failures with a remediation path.

data.boundary: An agent loop controls when one run continues, pauses, or stops; harness engineering changes the environment around that loop. It cannot guarantee that a model never fails, but it can expose recurring errors earlier, preserve evidence, and feed corrections into the next turn. Installing an SDK or writing a long instruction file does not create a reliable harness by itself.

lessonPractice.title: A frontend agent delivers a page that “looks done” three times, but the main button never works. Which change is harness engineering?

options.label: Have an independent evaluator complete the live flow, return failed steps and screenshots, and end only after it passes
options.feedback: Correct. This adds an environment that operates the page, produces failure evidence, and returns it to the next turn.

options.label: Only ask for more static screenshots and pass the page whenever they look complete
options.feedback: A static image proves that the page renders, not that its buttons, navigation, or end-to-end task work.

options.label: Add “carefully check every interaction” while still letting the agent judge its own work
options.feedback: A reminder adds no new source of evidence, so the same omission can survive another turn.

data.agentPrompt: Do not rebuild the feature yet. Describe the repeated failure as: observable evidence → missing environmental support → file, tool, or check to add → how the result returns to the next turn → what counts as passing. Propose the smallest harness first, then implement it and verify it with real evidence.
